description:
Income, poverty and employment: median household income and per capita income ([B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013), [B19301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19301)), the share of people below the poverty line and below twice it ([C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002)), the share of households receiving SNAP ([B22010](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B22010)), the unemployment rate as a share of the civilian labor force ([B23025](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B23025)), the household income distribution collapsed to 7 shares from under $25,000 to $200,000 or more ([B19001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19001)), and median earnings for workers with earnings ([B20002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B20002)) — plus, at every level but block groups, where the Census Bureau does not publish them, the Gini index of income inequality ([B19083](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19083)) and the poverty rate by age for children under 18 and adults 65 and over ([B17001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17001)), plus total population ([B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003)) and population density for context.

Curated indicators for all **33,791** ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The 5-year file is the only ACS release published for ZCTAs at all — [areas published](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/areas-published.html) lists the 5-digit ZCTA under the 5-year estimates and nowhere else.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

A ZIP Code Tabulation Area [is not a ZIP code](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/geography/guidance/geo-areas/zctas.html) — it is the Census Bureau's block-built approximation of a USPS 5-digit delivery area — and it nests in nothing, so `state` is NULL on every row and there is no prefix join to counties or tracts. Relating ZCTAs to other geographies is a spatial operation. The medians thin out: `median_hh_income` is NULL for **9.60%** of ZCTAs and `per_capita_income` for **3.26%**, because a ZCTA with few households has no publishable median.

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2020 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (GENZ2020, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. GENZ2020 and not GENZ2024 because no cartographic ZCTA file has been published since: the 2020-based ZCTAs are the current ones, and they are the vintage this release tabulates ([ACS geography boundaries by year](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/geography-boundaries-by-year/2024.html) gives 5-digit ZCTA as "2020 Census"). The ZCTA file is also the one boundary file in this catalog with no state attribute, which is why `state` is NULL here.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2020 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 17 ZCTAs in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. Two more, 11717 and 11798, have boundaries and no matching ACS row, both in Suffolk County, New York — the county whose 2024 re-delineation also leaves 14 tracts and 39 block groups without ACS rows elsewhere in this catalog. No ACS ZCTA row is dropped in the other direction: all 33,772 tabulated ZCTAs have a polygon. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of five at this geography. The other themes are [People & Education](../zcta-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../zcta-housing/collection.json), [Commuting & Connectivity](../zcta-connectivity/collection.json) and [Health, Disability & Income by Race](../zcta-wellbeing/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../zctas/collection.json), carries all 135 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. A ZCTA nests in nothing: it can cross county and state lines, so there is no prefix join from `geoid` to any other collection here, and `state` is NULL on every row. Relating ZCTAs to counties or tracts is a spatial operation (or a Census relationship file), not a string operation. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [counties](../../counties/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [places and CDPs](../../places/catalog.json) and [congressional districts](../../congressional-districts/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive is a census-geography pyramid built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo): z0–z5 are county polygons carrying the Census Bureau's own published county estimates, and z6–z12 are the ZIP Code Tabulation Areas themselves. ZCTAs do not nest inside counties, so the county band is orientation at national zooms — real county values — and not a roll-up of these features. Thinning this many polygons down to a national zoom would show a biased subset (small urban geographies drop first) rather than less data, so the coarse zooms step up to a coarser census geography instead of a thinned sample of this one. Every band carries the same column names, so one style expression classifies every zoom — but below z6 you are looking at counties, not ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and the values there are the Bureau's official estimates for those geographies, with their own meaning, rather than a visualization-only average: clicking a coarse feature identifies a real county by `geoid` and `name`. The `*_moe` columns are excluded from the tiles at every zoom — a margin of error is computed for one specific geography and cannot be carried across bands — while the `*_cv` columns are kept. Statistics come from the GeoParquet, never from the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

styles/child-poverty.title: Children below the poverty line
styles/child-poverty.description: Share of residents under 18 with income below the federal poverty line, pale pink to deep magenta — not published for block groups. Measured over all 31,348 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 2%/8%/15%/27%/38%, which fall at the 20th/40th/59th/80th/90th percentile of the national distribution. 7.23% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value.

styles/default.title: Median household income
styles/default.description: Median household income, viridis dark purple (low) through teal and green to yellow (high). Measured over all 30,547 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas with a published value: 7 classes with breaks at $45k/$60k/$72k/$87k/$120k/$160k, which fall at the 9th/29th/50th/70th/90th/97th percentile of the national distribution. 9.6% have no published value and draw in neutral gray rather than as a low value. 9.97% have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 and render faded — the estimate is real but its margin of error swamps it.

styles/gini.title: Income inequality (Gini index)
styles/gini.description: Gini index of household income inequality, 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality), navy (low) to gold (high) — not published for block groups. Measured over all 32,327 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 0.37/0.4/0.43/0.47/0.5, which fall at the 22nd/37th/57th/79th/89th percentile of the national distribution.

styles/poverty.title: People below the poverty line
styles/poverty.description: Share of residents with income below the federal poverty line, pale yellow to deep red. Measured over all 32,878 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 5%/9%/13%/19%/28%, which fall at the 19th/42nd/61st/80th/92nd percentile of the national distribution. 40.53% of ZIP Code Tabulation Areas have a coefficient of variation above 0.3 at this geography, too many to fade without washing the map out, so read pct_below_poverty_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single ZCTA.

styles/snap.title: Households receiving SNAP
styles/snap.description: Share of households that received SNAP (food stamps) in the past 12 months, cream to dark red. Measured over all 32,819 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 3%/7%/12%/17%/26%, which fall at the 19th/39th/62nd/77th/91st percentile of the national distribution.

styles/unemployment.title: Unemployment rate
styles/unemployment.description: Unemployed share of the civilian labor force, pale lilac to deep purple. Measured over all 32,807 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 1%/3%/4.5%/6.5%/10%, which fall at the 19th/39th/58th/77th/90th percentile of the national distribution.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2020 cartographic boundary file — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (1:500,000, national)
source-cartographic-boundaries.description: The geometry this collection joins onto, shoreline-clipped and generalized for mapping. Only the join key, the name parts and the land-area field are kept; reprojected from NAD83 to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. GENZ2020 is the only cartographic ZCTA edition the Census Bureau publishes, and the 2020-based ZCTAs are the vintage this ACS release tabulates; its fields are suffixed with the vintage (`GEOID20`, `ZCTA5CE20`, `ALAND20`) and carry no state, which is why `state` is NULL in this collection. Served by census.gov.

doc-geo-tallies.title: 2020 Census national geographic entity tallies
doc-geo-tallies.description: The published count of every geographic entity type, which this collection's row count is checked against: 33,791 ZCTAs (33,642 US + 132 Puerto Rico + 17 island areas), 19,734 incorporated places and 12,454 census designated places, 441 congressional districts (436 US including the DC delegate + 1 Puerto Rico + 4 island areas). Index page: https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/geo/tallies.html.

doc-zcta-about.title: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs) — Census Bureau
doc-zcta-about.description: What a ZCTA is and, more importantly, what it is not: the Bureau's own page on how ZCTAs are built from census blocks to approximate USPS 5-digit ZIP delivery areas, why they do not match ZIP codes, and why they do not nest in any other census geography.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 5-digit ZIP Code Tabulation Area code, e.g. `90210`. **Not a ZIP code**: a ZCTA is the Census Bureau's approximation of the area a USPS 5-digit ZIP delivery area covers, built from 2020 census blocks, and the two are not interchangeable (see the collection's known issues). ZCTAs do not nest in any other census geography — a ZCTA can cross county and state lines — so there is no prefix join to counties, tracts or states, and the first two characters are a postal region, not a state FIPS code. Matches `GEOID20`/`ZCTA5CE20` in the Census Bureau's 2020 cartographic boundary ZCTA file; the ACS `860Z200US` prefix is stripped.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: `'ZCTA5 ' || ZCTA5CE20` from the 2020 cartographic boundary ZCTA file — "ZCTA5 90210". A ZCTA has no containing geography to name it by, because it crosses county and state lines, and the Census Bureau publishes no other name for one; this is the label data.census.gov uses.

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Always NULL in this collection. A ZIP Code Tabulation Area is not inside any state: it approximates a USPS ZIP delivery area, which can cross state lines, the ACS publishes ZCTAs at the nation level only, and the 2020 cartographic boundary ZCTA file carries no state attribute (its fields are `ZCTA5CE20`, `AFFGEOID20`, `GEOID20`, `NAME20`, `LSAD20`, `ALAND20`, `AWATER20`). The column is kept so the schema matches the other collections; deriving a value from the first digits of the code would be wrong, because those are a postal region. To assign ZCTAs to states, do it spatially, and expect ties.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.06% of ZCTAs — the 19 ZCTAs that have a 2020 cartographic boundary but no row in the ACS tabulation (17 in the island areas, plus 11717 and 11798 in Suffolk County, New York).

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND20 / 1e6` from the 2020 cartographic boundary ZCTA file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars. Universe: households. Line 1 of [B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013), published as the Census Bureau publishes it. A median cannot be aggregated: there is no way to combine the medians of two block groups into the median of their union. **NULL on 9.60% of ZCTAs.** A ZCTA with few households has no publishable median — the rate sits between the tract (1.59%) and block-group (7.69%) rates because a rural ZCTA is large but a single-building urban one is tiny.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_hh_income` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_hh_income`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: per_capita_income
table:columns.description: Per capita income in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars — aggregate income divided by total population, so children and people with no income are in the denominator. Universe: total population. Line 1 of [B19301](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19301).

table:columns.name: per_capita_income_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `per_capita_income` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty
table:columns.description: Percent of the population below the federal poverty level — an income-to-poverty ratio under 1.00. Universe: population for whom poverty status is determined, which excludes institutionalized people, people in military group quarters and in college dormitories, and unrelated individuals under 15. Lines 2 ("Under .50") + 3 (".50 to .99") of [C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002) over line 1.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_below_poverty` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_below_poverty`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_below_2x_poverty
table:columns.description: Percent of the population with an income-to-poverty ratio under 2.00 — a common proxy for low income rather than deep poverty. Universe: population for whom poverty status is determined. Lines 2–7 of [C17002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.C17002) over line 1 (equivalently, everyone not in line 8, "2.00 and over").

table:columns.name: pct_below_2x_poverty_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_below_2x_poverty` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_snap

table:columns.name: median_earnings
table:columns.description: Median earnings in the past 12 months, in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars — wages, salary, and self-employment income, for people who have earnings. Universe: population 16 years and over with earnings in the past 12 months — a narrower universe than `median_hh_income`'s (households) or `per_capita_income`'s (total population): someone with no earnings, retired or unemployed, is outside it, so this is not comparable to either. Line 1 of [B20002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B20002) (Median Earnings in the Past 12 Months by Sex for the Population 16 Years and Over With Earnings), the combined-sex total; the male and female medians the table also publishes are not carried here.

table:columns.name: median_earnings_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_earnings` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_earnings_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_earnings`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: gini_index

Universe: households. The single line of [B19083](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19083) (Gini Index of Income Inequality), published as the Census Bureau publishes it, to 4 decimal places. **Not published for block groups** — B19083 carries no block-group rows in this release (measured against the cached `.dat` file), which is why there is no `gini_index` column in `bg-income`; see that collection's known issues.

table:columns.name: gini_index_moe

table:columns.name: pct_below_poverty_under_18
table:columns.description: Child poverty rate: percent of the population under 18 below the federal poverty level. Universe: population under 18 for whom poverty status is determined — narrower than `pct_below_poverty`'s all-ages universe, so the two percentages are not directly comparable. [B17001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17001) (Poverty Status in the Past 12 Months by Sex by Age) bins ages non-standardly; the six under-18 age labels ("Under 5 years" through "16 and 17 years") each appear once under the below-poverty branch and once under the at-or-above branch, for each sex. The numerator sums the 12 below-poverty lines for those labels (lines 4–9 male, 18–23 female); the denominator adds the matching 12 at-or-above lines (33–38 male, 47–52 female) to get the full under-18 population for whom poverty status is determined. **Not published for block groups** — B17001 carries no block-group rows in this release (measured); see `bg-income`'s known issues.

The numerator sums the 4 below-poverty lines for those labels (15, 16, 29, 30); the denominator adds the matching at-or-above lines (44, 45, 58, 59) to get the full 65-and-over population for whom poverty status is determined. **Not published for block groups** — B17001 carries no block-group rows in this release (measured); see `bg-income`'s known issues.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2020 cartographic boundary ZIP Code Tabulation Area file (GENZ2020, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the ZIP Code Tabulation Area into open water. GENZ2020 because the Census Bureau has published no cartographic ZCTA file since: the 2020-based ZCTAs are the current ones, and they are the vintage the ACS tabulates. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.
